questions.question: List the structures air passes through from the nose to the site of gas exchange, and state the three functions of the nasal cavity and the function of the cartilage rings and cilia in the trachea.
questions.expected_answer: Nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli. The nasal cavity filters air with hairs and mucus, warms it with its blood supply and moistens it. Cartilage rings keep the trachea open so it cannot collapse; cilia beat upward to sweep dust-laden mucus to the throat to be swallowed.

questions.question: Describe inhalation and exhalation at rest in terms of muscle action, chest volume, pressure and air movement.
questions.expected_answer: Inhalation: the diaphragm contracts and flattens and the external intercostal muscles contract, lifting the ribs up and out; chest volume increases; pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure; air flows in. Exhalation: the diaphragm relaxes and domes upward and the intercostals relax so the ribs fall; the elastic lungs recoil; chest volume decreases; pressure rises above atmospheric; air flows out.

questions.question: Compare inhaled and exhaled air for oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, water vapour and temperature, and explain how smoking causes emphysema and the smoker's cough.
questions.expected_answer: Oxygen falls from about 21 percent to about 16 percent; carbon dioxide rises from about 0,04 percent to about 4 percent; nitrogen stays about 78 percent; exhaled air carries more water vapour and is warmer, about 37 °C. Tar paralyses the cilia so mucus and dirt are not swept out and coughing must do the job; hot smoke and tar destroy alveolar walls so the alveoli merge into fewer, larger sacs with less surface area for gas exchange, causing permanent breathlessness, which is emphysema.
